title: Router Scoreboard (Per-Port Ordering)
constraints: A 1→4 router preserves order **per output port**, but packets to different ports interleave arbitrarily. Write `class router_scoreboard` with `add_input(pkt p)`, `add_output(int port, pkt p)`, `final_check()` and public counters `n_match, n_misroute, n_order, n_corrupt, n_missing, n_unknown`.

`add_output`: find the expected packet with the same `uid` (on any port) and remove it. Classify in this priority: it was expected on a different port → `n_misroute`; payload differs → `n_corrupt`; it isn't the **oldest** outstanding packet of its port → `n_order`; otherwise `n_match`. A uid that isn't outstanding anywhere → `n_unknown`.
`final_check()` sets `n_missing` = packets still outstanding (dropped by the router).
hints: Keep one queue of expected packets per destination port: `pkt exp_q[4][$]`.
Search by uid so that a misrouted or overtaking packet is still identified (and retired) correctly.
The ordering check is just 'is it at index 0 of its port's queue?'.
